**The gate, and what it was measured against**

work-unit · 2026-09-10

the milestone: [MUS-D-0152](../decisions.md#mus-d-0152)

the rule: [MUS-D-0153](../decisions.md#mus-d-0153)

what the rule also declines: [MUS-D-0154](../decisions.md#mus-d-0154)

how long it waits: [MUS-D-0155](../decisions.md#mus-d-0155)

why the pair is unavailable: [MUS-F-0122](../findings.md#mus-f-0122)

## Context

Milestone 8's build: a tool call the session is about to make is held in front of the owner, answered from the surface, and the terminal underneath is untouched.

**Against the real CLI, through Mustur's own adapter rather than the investigation's harness.** The session was started by "mustur session start" -- the same path the surface uses, carrying the same hook Mustur composes -- in manual permission mode, and given a prompt that needs one Bash call.

Allowed: Mustur was told the tool was Bash, the command was "touch gate-ran-it" and the mode was default; before the press the tool had not run and no dialog had been drawn; after the press the tool ran, no dialog was ever drawn, and the held file was gone. Denied, in a second session: the same up to the press, and after it the tool had still not run and the agent said so in its own words -- "The command was refused -- a check blocked it, so gate-ran-it was not created."

The terminal survived both. The pane took typed input after the exchange, and a second client attached over its own tmux socket, rendered the session, and typed into it.

**In the tests, without a CLI.** The gate's rule over nine cases, including the modes the CLI never prompts in and a session that gates nothing. The payloads investigation 0003 captured, including the quiet one where PreToolUse fires for a call nobody would have been asked about and the gate must decline it. What is not an ask: a sub-agent's own call, PostToolUse, a call with no identifier, junk. A press that arrives after the timeout, refused. An identifier that names a path, made safe. And over real tmux and a real socket: a call raised before the tab opens arrives on the hello frame, a press reaches a process blocked exactly as the hook blocks, a press for a call nothing holds is refused out loud, and a call whose hook was killed clears within a tick rather than covering the dialog the CLI drew in its place.

The first socket test was mutation-checked: with the server's lookup stubbed out it fails.

**What no test proves.** That the pop-up is usable on a phone, at the moment an agent is waiting -- which is 2c's last sentence and 5b's, and is the owner's to try. And that five minutes is the right number: MUS-D-0155 records the choice, not a measurement of how long a person actually takes.

## Method

docs/investigations/0003-harness for the CLI's own behaviour; the end-to-end runs were one session start and one prompt, answered by writing the same file the session view writes

## Measured

allow ran the tool with no dialog drawn; deny stopped it and the agent said so; the pane took input after both; a second client attached and typed

## Not measured

how long a person actually takes to answer, which is what MUS-D-0155's five minutes is a choice about rather than a measurement of

## Proven from a phone

2026-09-11, by the owner, in a session started in a prompting mode. They sent one prompt from mustur.devofpie.com, the pop-up reached their phone naming the tool and the command, and they pressed it. The pane carries the other half: the command ran and no dialog was ever drawn on it, so the press resolved the call rather than the timeout. Claude Code 2.1.268, which is a version none of the measurements above used
